purpose: Source-linked standards and solver applicability snapshot for research planning. This is not legal advice, a complete normative interpretation, a laboratory approval, a certification or a product performance claim.

status_legend.CURRENT_WITH_AMENDMENTS: Official issuing authority identifies a published standard and the listed addenda must be incorporated.
status_legend.CURRENT_PUBLISHED: Official issuing authority identifies a published current edition at snapshot date; applicability still needs checking.
status_legend.DRAFT_OR_ENQUIRY: Published for public comment or enquiry; not treated as a final normative edition.
status_legend.VERIFY_LOCALLY: Exact current edition, amendments, adoption, laboratory scope or jurisdictional applicability requires confirmation from the competent official catalogue/authority.
status_legend.PROGRAMME_REQUIREMENT: A product conformity/compliance programme document, not itself the technical test standard.
status_legend.RESEARCH_REFERENCE: Peer-reviewed literature or research context; not a normative test requirement.
status_legend.SOFTWARE_CANDIDATE: Potential simulation software; not independently validated for this armour use case.

entries.publisher: United States National Institute of Justice
entries.scope: Minimum performance requirements and test methods for ballistic-resistant body armour intended to protect the human torso against declared handgun/rifle protection categories. NIJ CTP scope must not be generalized to limbs, helmets, animals, backpacks, blankets, shields, accessories or other unqualified articles.
interpretation_limits: Incorporate all applicable addenda; do not cite only the base edition.
A test result is not NIJ compliance status unless all applicable CTP product, laboratory, workmanship, labelling and follow-up requirements are satisfied.
A change to the tested carrier, cover, panel, insert, size, closure, seam, lot or construction requires an explicit applicability/requalification decision.
A ballistic result does not establish fit, mobility, thermal comfort, durability, multi-hit behavior or medical injury reduction beyond the exact test scope.

entries.publisher: United States National Institute of Justice
entries.scope: Defines NIJ ballistic protection levels and associated test threats for use with equipment test standards. It is not, by itself, a product-performance test method or product certification.
interpretation_limits: Incorporate both published addenda.
Do not treat a protection-level label as a tested product result.
Do not translate legacy level labels into current categories without a versioned mapping.

entries.publisher: National Institute of Justice Compliance Testing Program
entries.scope: General requirements for products in the NIJ Product Conformity Assessment System.
interpretation_limits: Read with the applicable product-category scheme.
Do not infer compliance from a laboratory report without the applicable programme decision and product listing.

entries.publisher: National Institute of Justice Compliance Testing Program
entries.scope: Product conformity assessment scheme for ballistic body armour tested against NIJ Standard 0101.07.
interpretation_limits: Manufacturer participation, approved-laboratory testing, workmanship and labelling requirements, model listing and follow-up obligations are separate from a stand-alone test report.
NIJ states six follow-up inspections and testing over five years for a compliant model.
NIJ-approved labs must be independent third parties, meet NIST NVLAP and technical-scope requirements, and conduct NIJ compliance testing within the United States.

entries.publisher: United States National Institute of Justice
entries.scope: Separate torso-worn stab-resistant armour standard. Not interchangeable with ballistic resistance qualification.
interpretation_limits: Confirm the current edition, applicable programme status and exact product class before any current qualification claim.
Keep stab, slash and ballistic claims separate and bound to the exact method.

entries.publisher: South African Bureau of Standards (draft public-comment notice)
entries.scope: Draft minimum ballistic-resistance performance requirements for body armour intended to protect the wearer's torso. Government Gazette Notice 3339 of 2025 lists the draft for public comment with closing date 2025-08-27.
interpretation_limits: The Gazette notice establishes that this edition was a draft for comment; it does not establish final publication.
Do not treat the 20XX draft as a current normative edition.
Confirm the final published SABS edition, amendments, currentness and applicability in the SABS catalogue.

entries.scope: A South African ballistic-testing provider currently advertises SANS 1658:2025 for body-armour testing.
interpretation_limits: A vendor service webpage is not the SABS normative catalogue and does not establish the exact published edition or currentness.
Resolve the discrepancy against the official SABS catalogue and obtain the complete normative standard before relying on it.
The provider's claim of SANAS approval must be checked against the current SANAS certificate and schedule for the exact test method and scope.

entries.edition: Current certificate and scope schedule required
entries.scope: Competence and scope of a testing laboratory for the exact ballistic test method and product class.
interpretation_limits: Accreditation is scope-specific; general ISO/IEC 17025 status is not proof that the laboratory is accredited for a particular armour method.
A SANAS-accredited laboratory is not automatically an NIJ-approved Compliance Testing Program laboratory.
Verify certificate number, active status, expiry, test method, specimen/product scope, location and any relevant restrictions.

research_references.title: Aramid Fibre Composites for Ballistic Impact Protection: A Mechanistic Review of Recent Advances
research_references.use: Mechanism and architecture literature review. Candidate design families are not established performance recommendations.
limits: Review synthesis is not independent qualification of a new Luminous design.
Hybridization and architecture effects are configuration-dependent; inappropriate choices can reduce ballistic performance.

research_references.title: Three-dimensional woven fabric composites under ballistic impact: A systematic review of multiscale modeling strategies from fiber to structural scale
limits: The review reports no broad, independently validated multiscale predictive framework across architectures and impact regimes.
It identifies calibration-dependent reported accuracy, missing dynamic interfacial fracture-toughness data and a near-absence of validated multi-hit models.
Do not generalize a result for one architecture or regime to all 3D woven designs.

research_references.title: Soldiers experience fit issues, musculoskeletal pain, and equipment and mobility interference with military body armour
research_references.use: Fit, anthropometry, pain and mobility measurement rationale.
limits: Study population and military context must not be treated as universal estimates for all wearers.
A literature finding does not replace local anthropometric, wearer-centred research under approved protocols.

solver_candidates.domain_claimed_by_project: Explicit finite element simulation for crash, impact and highly nonlinear dynamic events.
solver_candidates.currentness_note: Community continuation of the OpenRadioss code base; latest published package page observed 2026-10-11.
limits: Not validated by this record for the exact body-armour materials, architecture, impact regime or injury endpoint.
Every model law, contact/interface model, mesh/time step, boundary condition and failure mechanism requires case-specific verification, calibration and independent validation.
AGPL-3.0 licensing requires a separate architecture/licensing review before use or distribution.
No solver output may be treated as physical proof or certification.

required_reverification_before_claim: Retrieve the current normative text and addenda from the official issuing body.
Re-check the NIJ Compliant Products List and current CTP documents for the exact model.
For South Africa, resolve SANS 1658 publication/currentness through SABS and the competent procurement/approval authority.
Retrieve the laboratory's active accreditation certificate and scope schedule for the exact method.
Bind the tested article, size, carrier, cover, panels, lot, construction and conditioning to the evidence.
Do not make product-performance, medical, certification or compliance claims from this research crosswalk alone.
